snippet.title: Al Capone's Bloody Business — A Chicago Stories Documentary
snippet.description:
During the Prohibition-era 1920s, a young man named Al Capone succeeded his mentor, Johnny Torrio, to run the Chicago Outfit. An Italian-American crime syndicate first established by “Big Jim” Colosimo at the turn of the century, the Outfit amassed an estimated $100 million in revenue – more than $1.5 billion today – through its nearly 200 brothels, illegal alcohol production and sales, gambling, and racketeering. For several years, the mob had a chokehold on Chicago politics, influencing elections through intimidation and violence and working in cahoots with the aldermen who ran the city’s political machine. This quintessentially Chicago story traces the powerful criminal enterprise from its inception through its 1920s heyday and to its gradual demise. At the center of it all, wearing a sleek fedora and a knowing smirk, was Capone – “Public Enemy No. 1” – and one of America’s most notorious gangsters.

snippet.title: CORLEONE : L'histoire du Parrain le plus Dangereux de la Mafia italienne – Documentaire -  AT
snippet.description:
Comment un simple fils de paysan sicilien est-il devenu le parrain le plus redouté d’Europe ? 👋 + de documentaires histoire  👉 http://bit.ly/3lqyFpY 🙏 Abonnez vous !

00:00 LE POUVOIR PAR LE SANG
01:17:35 LA CHUTE 

01 - LE POUVOIR PAR LE SANG : Le film de Mosco Levi Boucault retrace en deux parties le destin hors du commun de Toto Riina (1930-2017), fils d’un paysan pauvre de Corleone, un bourg sicilien à 60 km de Palerme, devenu le parrain des parrains de la Mafia sicilienne, Cosa Nostra. Une histoire ni mythique ni romantique, mais une équipée sauvage et sanguinaire, une trame quasi shakespearienne, cadencée par des centaines de meurtres, autour de l’éternel conflit entre la soif de pouvoir et la vertu de la loi. Appuyé notamment sur les témoignages inédits et saisissants de tueurs mafieux repentis, ce premier volet retrace l’ascension irrésistible et impitoyable d’un homme roué et ambitieux, utilisant le meurtre et l’intrigue pour entrer dans le « triumvirat » qui dirige Cosa Nostra. A partir de là, il instaure un climat de terreur en éliminant ceux qui s’opposent à lui au sein de Cosa Nostra et en assassinant, pour la première fois dans l’histoire de la mafia, des représentants des institutions qui le combattent : journalistes, magistrats, hommes politiques, policiers. Une escalade qui culmine en 1982 avec le meurtre du général dalla Chiesa envoyé par Rome pour rétablir l’ordre en Sicile. Toto Riina règne alors sur la Sicile en toute impunité. 

02 - LA CHUTE : L’assassinat en 1982 du général dalla Chiesa est le crime de trop. Directement défié, le parquet de Palerme lance sur les traces de Toto Riina une équipe de magistrats qui s’attaque aux hommes d’affaires et aux politiciens jusqu’alors intouchables du fait de leurs liens avec la mafia. Toto Riina réagit en faisant tuer le juge Chinicci par un attent@t à la voiture piégée. Deux jeunes juges palermitains, Giovanni Falcone et Paolo Borsellino, font alors de la lutte contre la mafia le combat de leur vie. Grâce notamment au témoignage d’un ancien rival de Riina résolu à se venger, ils finissent par lancer des centaines de mandats d’arrêt contre Cosa Nostra. En 1986, et malgré le climat de terreur entretenu par Toto Riina, toujours en cavale, s’ouvre à Palerme le « maxi-procès » de 475 prévenus. Il aboutira à de très lourdes condamnations, dont la perpétuité par contumace pour Toto Riina. Verdict historique confirmé contre toute attente en appel et en cassation. De rage, Riina organise en 1992 deux attent@ts meurtriers à la dynamite contre les juges Falcone et Borsellino. Une double tragédie ressentie dans le souvenir des Siciliens comme un 11 septembre avant la lettre. Toto Riina est enfin arrêté en 1993, et mourra en prison. Cette guerre sanglante s’est déroulée sur une île sombre et solaire, en Europe, entre 1977 et 1994.

snippet.title: "Little Nicky" Scarfo: The Most Violent Boss in Mafia History? | S1E2 | Underworld Histories
snippet.description:
By the end of the 20th century, the Philadelphia mafia is in big trouble. The rules and traditions which for almost a century held together the darkest and most sinister organization in America, have been slowly unraveling -- nowhere more so than on the streets of South Philadelphia. In the process, Omerta, the mafia's once sacrosanct code of secrecy is shattered, revealing a dysfunctional crime family, riddled with factional infighting, conspiracies and murder. Under Angelo Bruno the Philadelphia Crime Family was among the most powerful mafia families in the United States. But his murder in 1980 signaled the beginning of a violent mob war and struggle for power. Gone are the traditional ways of the mafia, to be replaced with a younger generation out to make fast money, encapsulated by the values of greed and entrepreneurship. But while this new breed of mobster was looking for ways to make a quick buck, another battle is being waged. The weapon of choice is the 'turncoat', a mafia member bought out by the FBI in exchange for information and leniency. Armed with a new generation of surveillance technology and with their own lives under threat from jealous rivals, their actions would trigger the decimation of the Philadelphia mafia once and for all.

Throughout the bustling cities of Philadelphia, Las Vegas, Miami, Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, London, San Francisco, Tijuana, Brooklyn, Tampa and Montreal, a multitude of crime syndicates and gangs make up a diverse and brutal underworld. Each episode of this revealing docu-series examines one great city from the underbelly up and tells the story of how its geography, history and culture have made it fertile ground for the organized crime groups that call it home.

snippet.title: Toto Riina: The Bloodiest Godfather in Mafia History | Documentary History - AT
snippet.description:
What turns a poor Sicilian farmer into the most feared Mafia boss in modern history? 🔔 Subscribe and join us on this journey around the world → https://bit.ly/WorldView-Documentary

00:00 POWER THROUGH BLOODSHED
01:17:35 THE DOWNFALL

This is the story of the rise and fall of Toto Riina, through interviews of prosecutors, judges, police officers, lawyers and his own inside-men who are now repentant and have accepted to cooperate with justice.

In May 1992, a motorway near Palermo, Sicily, explodes killing Judge Falcone and several people of his inner circle, marking the climax in the war between the Italian State and the Cosa Nostra that killed thousands. One year later, after a 25-year manhunt, Toto Riina, the Godfather of all Godfathers, is finally arrested and brought to justice in a historic trial.
 
In a 5-year in depth investigation, discover how a young rural mobster took power in the 1970’s over the Cosa Nostra, Sicily’s legendary mafia, torturing and killing each competitor one by one, becoming the most feared and violent organized-crime leader ever. He broke the mafia code by declaring war on the Italian State, multiplying assassinations and establishing terror among government, police, the judicial systems and the Sicilian people.

POWER THROUGH BLOODSHED: Mosco Levi Boucault’s film retraces over two parts the extraordinary destiny of Totò Riina (1930-2017), the son of a peasant from Corleone, a small Sicilian town 60km from Palermo, who became the “capo de tutti capi” of the local Mafia, Cosa Nostra.  It is a tale that is neither mythical nor romantic, a wild and bloody adventure, almost Shakespearian in its drama, dotted with hundreds of killings around the eternal conflict between the thirst for power and the rule of law. Mainly based on exclusive and gripping testimony of underworld killers-turned-informers, the first part tracks the irresistible and merciless ascension of a cunning and ambitious man, who killed and schemed his way into the triumvirate which ran Cosa Nostra. From then on, he imposed a reign of terror, eliminating anyone who opposed him within Cosa Nostra and, for the first time in the history of the Mafia, assassinating representatives of institutions that were fighting it, including magistrates, police officers, politicians and journalists. This escalation culminated in 1982 with the slaying of General Alberto Dalla Chiesa, sent by Rome re-establish order in Sicily. Totò Riina then ruled over the whole island with impunity.

THE DOWNFALL: The assassination of Dalla Chiesa in 1982 was one crime too many. Targeted directly, the Palermo prosecutor’s office set a team of magistrates on Totò Riina’s case, going after the businessmen and politicians who had previously been untouchable thanks to their mafia links. 

Totò Riina responded by having the magistrate Rocco Chinnici killed in a car-bomb attack. Two young magistrates from Palermo, Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino, then made bringing down the Mafia their sole aim in life. Thanks to the testimony of one of Riina’s former rivals bent on revenge, they issued hundreds of arrest warrants against Cosa Nostra. In 1986, despite the climate of terror which Riina maintained whilst on the run, a “maxi trial” was held in Palermo with 475 accused. It resulted in some very heavy sentences, including a life term for Riina, pronounced in his absence. Against all expectations, this historic verdict was confirmed both on appeal and at the supreme court. Enraged, Riina in 1992 organized two bombings which killed respectively Falcone and Borsellino – a double tragedy that sticks in the memory of Sicilians like 9/11 does for New Yorkers. Totò Riina was finally arrested in 1993, and would die in prison. This bloody battle played out in Europe between 1977 and 1994, on a sun-kissed island with a very dark side.

snippet.title: Meet the Most Violent Mob Boss in Mafia History
snippet.description:
Nicodemo “Nicky” Scarfo wasn’t just a Mafia boss — he was a ruler who governed through fear, paranoia, and relentless violence. As the head of the Philadelphia crime family in the 1980s, Scarfo oversaw one of the bloodiest eras in American Mafia history, ordering hits not only on rivals, but on his own allies.

In this documentary-style deep dive, we trace Scarfo’s rise from a small-time South Philadelphia thug to one of the most feared mob bosses of the modern era. From his first killing in a diner to the brutal murders that shattered the Philadelphia Mafia, this is the story of how violence became both Scarfo’s weapon — and his downfall.

Featuring historically accurate accounts, key assassinations, internal Mafia wars, and the federal prosecutions that finally brought him down, this video explores why even other mobsters believed Nicky Scarfo went too far.

If you’re fascinated by true crime, Mafia history, and the dark side of organized crime, this is a story you don’t want to miss.

snippet.description:

In this documentary, we expose the true Miami underworld that Hollywood turned into Tony Montana:
• How the 1980 Mariel boatlift flooded South Florida with 125,000 Cuban refugees, hidden among them thousands of violent felons released from Castro’s prisons
 • Why the Medellin cartel chose Miami as its primary entry point into the United States and how 70% of all American cocaine flowed through a single city
 • The bloody rise of Griselda Blanco, La Madrina, the female cartel boss who pioneered motorcycle assassinations and ordered over 200 murders
 • How real-life kingpins like Mario Tabraue, Sal Magluta, and Willy Falcon built billion-dollar empires that inspired Oliver Stone’s screenplay
 • The $5 billion cash surplus at the Miami Federal Reserve and how laundered drug money built the modern Miami skyline
 • Why the federal South Florida Task Force won the battle but lost the war, pushing the cocaine trade into Mexico and birthing today’s cartels

- Griselda Blanco

snippet.title: The Prince of the Mafia: The Wild Story of the Franzese Family (Documentary)
snippet.description:
#mafia #michaelfranzese #organizedcrime
Documentary about the Franzese family

The Franzese family is one of the most iconic families in the history of organized crime in the United States, with an influence that spanned several decades. In this video, we dive deep into their fascinating story, centered around two legendary figures: John “Sonny” Franzese and his son, Michael Franzese.

John Franzese, the ruthless underboss of the Colombo crime family, ruled the New York underworld with an iron fist for years, becoming a key figure in the Italian-American Mafia. Despite numerous trials, prison sentences, and repeated attempts to bring him down, Sonny remained an almost untouchable figure in organized crime. Discover how this feared man  considered one of the oldest living mafiosi until his death at the age of 103   managed to maintain his power while navigating the traps of the justice system.

His son, Michael Franzese, nicknamed “the Prince of the Mafia,” followed in his father’s footsteps and became a captain in the Colombo family. At the height of his power, he was making millions of dollars through illegal activities, most notably the famous gasoline tax fraud scheme. Yet Michael defied all expectations by leaving the Mafia in the 1990s   an extremely rare decision in a brutal world where the usual outcome is prison or death.

In this video, we explore how he managed to escape that dangerous life, avoid Mafia retaliation, and reinvent himself as a public speaker and media personality  especially through his highly successful YouTube channel.

The rise, fall, and redemption of Michael Franzese offer a rare and compelling look into the hidden world of the Mafia, revealing the sacrifices, betrayals, and personal struggles behind the image of power and glory. Through interviews, archival footage, and in-depth analysis, we break down the complex legacy of the Franzese family and how they shaped the history of American organized crime.

If you are fascinated by the Mafia, stories of power and redemption, and the behind-the-scenes world of organized crime, this video is for you. Don’t miss this deep dive into the Franzese dynasty.

snippet.description:
The Rise and Fall of Fat Tony Salerno: America’s Richest Mafia Kingpin
The Rise and Fall of Fat Tony Salerno: America’s Richest Mafia Kingpin
The Rise and Fall of Fat Tony Salerno: America’s Richest Mafia Kingpin

Discover the complete untold story of Anthony “Fat Tony” Salerno – the cigar-chomping East Harlem mobster Fortune Magazine once named America’s most powerful and wealthiest gangster.
Born in 1911 on the tough streets of Italian Harlem, Fat Tony rose from small-time street operator to control one of New York’s largest numbers rackets – an illegal lottery empire that reportedly grossed up to $50 million a year at its peak. He dominated loansharking, extortion, and construction bid-rigging, influencing everything from Manhattan skyscrapers to national labor unions.
By the early 1980s, Salerno had become the public front boss of the powerful Genovese Crime Family, secretly shielding the real power behind the scenes while sitting on the Mafia Commission – the secret ruling council of New York’s Five Families.
This gripping true crime documentary covers his full life: his meteoric rise through the 116th Street Crew, lavish lifestyle with a Miami Beach mansion and sprawling upstate horse farm, the legendary Palma Boys Social Club headquarters, and his dramatic downfall in the historic Mafia Commission Trial.
Indicted in 1985 alongside other top bosses, convicted under RICO in 1986 and sentenced to 100 years (plus another 70 years in 1988 for construction racketeering), Fat Tony spent his final days behind bars. He died in federal prison in 1992 at age 80.
If you love Mafia documentaries, American organized crime history, and stories of power, greed, and betrayal like John Gotti, Vincent Gigante, or Paul Castellano – this is a must-watch.

Discover how publicity, greed, narcotics trafficking, informants, and internal rivalries weakened the Five Families from within and ultimately changed the future of organized crime in New York City.
